subject: Unit economics follow-up: token volumes & target $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Unit economics details from today's call

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can size a recommended pricing approach:

- Quick recap: demo + architecture fit for your fraud-scoring assistant. You liked caching and batching ideas for latency-sensitive flows.
- Asks from our side to finalize pricing:
  1) Expected monthly token volume (prompt+response) by feature (scoring API, user-facing chat, nightly re-scores). If you have a CSV export, that’s perfect.
  2) Target unit economics: do you have a target $/1M tokens or $/monthly-active-user that finance uses for vendor selection?
  3) Budget range for year-1 inference spend (annualized) and any procurement timing constraints.
  4) Typical latency SLO per feature (p95) and acceptable degradation trade-offs vs cost.

I attached a short unit_econ_template.xlsx to make this quick — it maps tokens -> $/1M -> gross margin under different CAC assumptions.

If you can send rough numbers by Tue EOD (Mar 10) we’ll run a short model and propose a price ladder (hosted vs dedicated vs reserved) and a recommended rollout (canary -> scale).

Thanks — talk soon,

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (555) 212-0910
https://redwood.ai

Attachment: unit_econ_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Unit economics details from today's call

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below (we'll follow up with a CSV export from our analytics team later today):

1) Estimated monthly token volumes (combined prompt+response):
   - Fraud scoring API (real-time): 120M tokens/month
   - Agent chat (support assistants): 45M tokens/month
   - Nightly re-score batch jobs: 200M tokens/month
   => Total: ~365M tokens/month

2) Target unit economics: Finance has been using $2,500 per 1M tokens as an internal benchmark for vendor evaluation (this includes model cost + infra + margin). Their target for vendor spend is closer to $1,200–$1,800 per 1M if support/quality is comparable.

3) Budget range: For year-1 we can commit to ~$350k–$650k inference spend depending on price/discount structure and whether we use a dedicated pool. Procurement target: contract signed by end of Q2.

4) Latency SLOs:
   - Fraud scoring API: p95 < 150ms (real-time)
   - Agent chat: p95 < 400ms
   - Nightly jobs: throughput-focused, latency not critical

Cc'ing our finance alias for visibility. We'll send the CSV and a short product usage breakdown this afternoon.

Cheers,
Tom Harris
Head of Platform, FintechX
tom.harris@fintechx.com | +1-415-555-0199
FintechX

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Unit economics details from today's call

Tom — really helpful, thanks. A few clarifying questions so we can run a modeled proposal that maps to your $/1M target:

- Volume profile: is the 120M for fraud scoring dominated by short prompts (<=64 tokens) and short responses (<=32 tokens)? If so, effective tokens/req will be low which changes batching benefits.
- For the nightly re-scores (200M) do you expect them to run in a 2–4 hour window or spread across the night? That matters for whether a dedicated reserved pool is better than burst capacity on hosted.
- CAC/payback: what's your current CAC per new customer for the product these features enable? For example, if a feature adds $X revenue per MAU, we can compare gross margin vs inference spend to compute payback. If you don't have exact CAC, a top-line percent margin target (e.g., 30–40% contribution margin after inference) helps us tune recommendations.

We will upload a short model that translates tokens -> $/1M under three scenarios: hosted (on-demand), reserved dedicated (committed with discount), and private (VPC) — with recommended batch/caching settings to hit your $1,200–$1,800 target.

If it's useful, I can run two quick worked examples: (A) prioritize fraud scoring latency (higher $/1M), (B) prioritize cost for nightly re-scores (lower $/1M, more aggressive batching). Which would you like first?

Plan: once you confirm the few clarifications and send the CSV, we'll share the scenario model by Tue EOD and propose a short mutual action plan (MVP -> pilot -> scale).

Best,
— Marissa

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FintechX - Finance Team <finance@fintechx.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Unit economics details from today's call

Marissa —

Answers inline and attaching the CSV export (fintechx_volume_estimates.csv):

- Fraud scoring token sizes: average prompt 48 tokens, average response 24 tokens (short). Expect >85% of calls to be sub-100 tokens.
- Nightly re-scores: run in a rolling 6-hour window (midnight–6am PT). We have some flexibility to shift to longer windows if cost reductions are material.
- CAC/payback: our finance lead says CAC for the core product is ~$1,100 per new paid customer. We typically look for payback within 9–12 months. Contribution margin targets: 25–35% after infra & inference.

We'd prefer you start with option (A) — prioritize fraud scoring latency with a cost-aware plan for other workloads.

Thanks — attached and cc'ing finance.

Tom

Attachment: fintechx_volume_estimates.csv (CSV - token volumes by feature and month)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Unit economics details from today's call

Tom — perfect, this is exactly what we need. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) Aditya will model two price scenarios and run the unit-econ template vs your CAC/payback assumptions:
   - Scenario A (latency-first): dedicated pool for fraud scoring (p95 <150ms), targeted caching for chat; modeled $/1M after discounts.
   - Scenario B (cost-first): hosted + aggressive batching for nightly re-scores; estimate blended $/1M.
2) We'll deliver a short deck + spreadsheet by Tue EOD (Mar 10) that shows: $/1M, gross margin impact, CAC payback window, and recommended rollout.
3) If numbers look good we propose a 3-month pilot (discounted committed capacity) to validate production latency and unit economics before a larger dedicated commitment.

I'll loop with Rishi to schedule a 30-min review on Wed to walk through the model and get feedback from your finance lead. Rishi — can you join at 10am PT Wed?

Tom — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll be in touch with the modeled scenarios shortly.

Best regards,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (555) 212-0910
